alerts.reason: ACI's consolidated revenue fell 3.22% year over year in December and 2.16% in March, supporting a June forecast above -5%. Changes in tax due dates shifted Biller transaction volumes between periods. With March only 2.84 percentage points above the threshold, an unfavorable shift in the September comparison could push the decline to 5% (A–C).

Take-Two's reported revenue swung from a 7.44% year-over-year decline in December to 10.37% growth in March. The August 2020 launch of PGA TOUR 2K21 contributed to bookings growth and first enters the year-over-year comparison in the September quarter. That timing supports a forecast above -5% in June followed by a decline of at least 5% in September (B).

Fastenal's net sales growth slowed from 6.35% in December to 3.66% in March. Improving manufacturing and construction demand supports a June result above -5%, but demand for pandemic-related PPE had already begun to ease, and excess mask supply prompted a write-down. A further drop in PPE sales could outweigh gains in traditional products by September (A–C).

First Solar's net sales swung from -56.46% year over year in December to +50.98% in March. Higher third-party module volume supports a June forecast above -5%. Three project sales also drove the March increase, and construction at GA Solar 4 was substantially complete in 2020. With fewer project sales to supplement module revenue, September sales could fall at least 5% year over year (A–B).
